title: Theta Training
subtitle: Training slower rhythms with careful state control
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating theta training within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain theta training without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in theta training.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to theta training.

sections.explainSimply: Theta-range activity is often linked with drowsiness, memory operations and internal attention depending on location and task.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: A theta target has different meanings in frontal-midline task activity, posterior drowsiness and artifact-contaminated scalp EEG.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Protocols should define frequency, site, reference and behavioural state. Broad claims that theta is simply “creativity” or “pathology” are misleading.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Choosing a camera lens: every method emphasises some information and introduces its own distortions.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand theta training to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Rewarding drowsiness can be mistaken for cognitive training.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using theta training predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Rewarding drowsiness can be mistaken for cognitive training. Evidence classification: theoretical and task-dependent; mixed clinical evidence.
